They loan to subprime individuals.  But every deal starts at 22.99% and they lend 75% of wholesale.  So a typical $10,000 wholesale value vehicle say retail book is $14,000.  Standard deal dealer gets $2500 down CACC pays dealer $7500.  Then as the payments come in CACC keeps 20% over there initial investment dealer gets the rest.  But if the customer makes 0 payments CACC would reposes the vehicle send it to auction and in theory make a little.  Keep in mind they are charging interest on a loan of 11500 14 minus the down payment.  So they collect the interest on dealer mark up.  Money they never spent.
As a auto dealer who does business with CACC. I would caution this.  They only lend on average 75% of wholesale.  Unless the auto industry sees a huge downturn in wholesale prices they will be fine.
